kingdom.summary: This is a green, rooted plant that makes its own food, which puts it in Plantae. Chromista photosynthesizers (kelps, diatoms) are brownish or golden, fungi don't photosynthesize and have chitin walls, and protozoa are mostly microscopic single cells.

options.47170: Fungi (including lichens) cannot photosynthesize on their own; they absorb food from their surroundings. Their cell walls contain chitin, and most grow as networks of thread-like hyphae, showing up as mushrooms, moulds, brackets or crusts.
options.48222: Chromista includes kelps and other brown seaweeds, diatoms and water moulds. Photosynthetic members use chlorophylls a and c, plus brownish pigments such as fucoxanthin, so they look olive-brown or golden rather than grass-green.
options.47686: Protozoa are mostly single-celled organisms such as amoebae and slime moulds, which feed by engulfing or absorbing food. They lack cellulose walls and chloroplasts and are usually microscopic, though slime moulds can form visible blobs.
options.47126: Plants are multicellular organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis, using chloroplasts with chlorophylls a and b. Their cell walls are made of cellulose and they store energy as starch. Most are green and rooted in place.

phylum.summary: Huge leaves and a stout flower stalk can only be supported by vascular tissue. Liverworts are tiny non-vascular plants, while green algae and red algae (Rhodophyta) are mostly aquatic and have no true roots, stems or leaves.

options.64615: Liverworts are small non-vascular plants that are either flat, lobed thalli or leafy shoots with leaves in neat rows. Their spore capsules sit on short-lived, translucent stalks and they lack true roots.
options.50863: Green algae (Chlorophyta) are mostly aquatic, from single cells to sheets like sea lettuce. They share plant pigments but have no roots, stems, leaves or vascular tissue.
options.211194: Vascular plants have xylem and phloem, internal tubes that carry water and sugars, letting them grow tall with true roots, stems and leaves. The large, long-lived plant you see is the spore- or seed-producing generation.
options.57774: Red algae are mostly marine seaweeds coloured red, pink or purplish by the pigment phycoerythrin. They have no vascular tissue, roots or flowers, and are usually found attached to rocks in the sea.

class.summary: The large leaves have parallel-running veins coming off a central midrib, they rise from the base with sheathing stalks, and there is no woody growth: monocot traits. Ferns and lycophytes reproduce by spores, and conifers make cones.

options.47163: Monocots typically have one seed leaf, leaves with parallel veins (often long and strap-like with a sheathing base), flower parts in threes, scattered vascular bundles and fibrous roots.
options.121943: Ferns reproduce by spores, usually made in clusters (sori) on the underside of the fronds. New fronds unroll as fiddleheads, and they produce no flowers or seeds.
options.47623: Lycophytes (clubmosses, spikemosses, quillworts) have small leaves with a single unbranched vein. They reproduce by spores, often in cone-like tips, and never produce flowers or seeds.
options.136329: Conifers bear naked seeds on the scales of woody cones and have needle- or scale-like leaves. They never produce flowers or fruit, and most are evergreen trees or shrubs.

order.summary: The flowers are packed onto a fleshy spike (spadix) wrapped by a showy hood (spathe), a hallmark of the aroids in Alismatales, which is full of wetland plants. Poales have chaffy wind-pollinated flowers, Commelinales have 3 coloured petals, and Arecales are palms.

options.48073: Alismatales are mostly wetland and aquatic plants: aroids with a spadix (fleshy flower spike) wrapped in a spathe (hood-like bract), water-plantains with 3 white petals, and submerged pondweeds and seagrasses.
options.47162: Poales are grass-like plants with narrow, parallel-veined leaves and small, usually wind-pollinated, chaffy or brownish flowers. Sedges, rushes, cattails and pineapples (bromeliads) belong here.
options.49146: Commelinales (spiderworts, pickerelweeds) have flowers with 3 green sepals and 3 coloured, often blue or purple, short-lived petals. They are mainly tropical and warm-temperate.
options.48866: Arecales are the palms: woody, usually unbranched trunks topped by large fan- or feather-shaped leaves. They are tropical and warm-temperate and none are native to BC.

family.summary: Araceae has a spadix of tiny flowers enclosed or backed by a spathe, and broad leaves; it now also includes the tiny floating duckweeds. Ruppiaceae and Hydrocharitaceae are mostly submerged water plants, and Juncaginaceae have grass-like leaves and slender spikes of tiny green flowers.

options.61091: Ruppiaceae (widgeon-grass) are submerged plants of brackish water with thread-like leaves and tiny flowers on a stalk that often coils after flowering.
options.50361: Hydrocharitaceae (waterweeds, tape-grass, frogbit) are aquatic, usually submerged, with flowers emerging from a pair of bracts; Elodea has small leaves in whorls.
options.60266: Juncaginaceae (arrowgrasses) have fleshy, grass-like basal leaves and long, slender spikes of small greenish flowers. Common in salt marshes and wet meadows.
options.48536: Araceae: flowers tiny and crowded on a fleshy spike (spadix), usually with a large leaf-like or coloured bract (spathe). Leaves are often broad with netted veins. Includes the floating duckweeds.

genus.summary: Lysichiton is a big wetland plant with a short stout spadix and a large yellow or white spathe, followed by enormous paddle-shaped leaves in a basal rosette. Spirodela and Lemna are tiny floating duckweeds, and Arum has arrow-shaped leaves and a spadix tipped with a bare club.

options.57869: Spirodela (greater duckweed) is a floating frond only 3-10 mm across, usually purplish underneath, with several rootlets per frond. Rarely flowers.
options.51609: Arum (lords-and-ladies) has arrow-shaped leaves and a spathe wrapped around a spadix that ends in a club-shaped sterile tip; berries red. Eurasian; grown in gardens.
options.48729: Lysichiton: stout, rhizome-rooted plant of swamps; a cylindrical spadix of many perfect flowers inside a large hood-like spathe in early spring, then giant basal leaves up to about 1.5 m long.
options.54519: Lemna (duckweeds) are tiny floating fronds, a few millimetres across, each with a single rootlet. They form green carpets on still water.

species.summary: The spathe colour settles it: western skunk cabbage has a bright yellow spathe and the familiar skunky smell, and is native to BC. The Asian white skunk cabbage has a white spathe and is mostly grown in gardens here. The two Lemna options are tiny floating or submerged duckweeds, a different genus of the same family.

options.147285: Lysichiton camtschatcensis: white spathe up to about 40 cm, smaller overall; odour variable (sometimes sweet or none). Native to Kamchatka, the Kurils, Sakhalin and northern Japan; a garden plant in BC.
options.48537: Lysichiton americanus: bright yellow spathe around a greenish-yellow spadix in early spring; leaves up to 1.5 m; strong skunky smell. Common in swamps and wet forests west of the Coast-Cascade Mountains.
options.77656: Lemna turionifera is a tiny floating duckweed: a frond a few millimetres across with a single rootlet, which makes dormant overwintering buds (turions). Nothing like a large plant with a spathe.
options.77655: Lemna trisulca (star or ivy-leaved duckweed) floats just below the surface as translucent, stalked fronds joined in branching, criss-cross chains. A tiny aquatic plant, not a big swamp herb.
